name: CA-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Polymarket prices McGuire at ~95% to win
McGuire has outraised Gallagher and holds an outside-spending edge
Gallagher's incumbency provides only a modest offset
model.rationale: The redrawn North State district leans Democratic by seven points, and McGuire's fundraising and outside-spending advantage plus market pricing near 95% point to a clear Democratic edge. Gallagher's incumbency trims the margin slightly but not enough to change the category.
model.watch: Any credible general-election polling showing Gallagher running close, or a major outside-spending surge on his behalf, would move this toward Lean D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 1st District became markedly more Democratic after redistricting, with a partisan lean of about seven points toward Democrats. State Senator Mike McGuire, a well-known figure in the North State, faces incumbent Assemblyman James Gallagher, who holds the seat's Republican lineage but now represents a district tilted against his party.

McGuire has raised more money than Gallagher and benefits from outside support, while Gallagher's incumbency is his main asset. Prediction markets price McGuire as a heavy favorite, and no independent ratings or polls contradict that picture. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with a wide but not extreme expected margin.
